For example, scalar advection with a flux routine F(q_l,q_r)=q_l+ε has finite reference and physical-flux error bounds even when q_l=q_r, but fails Method.consistent for ε≠0. The restriction is reduced applicability, not stronger theorem content. Adjudication must determine whether it is acceptable within the exact selected capability scope.

rationale: The physical signs, cell-volume normalization, neighboring-state assignments, information-only pipeline, distinction between exact and numerical fluxes, finite-slab conservation semantics, and conditional error propagation all survive direct inspection. The inherited rectangle interpretation is relevant because (1.10) explicitly underlies this workflow; it does not authorize additional unrelated claims. Coordinator Q7 supports the conditional quantitative treatment, but does not explicitly select exact equal-state consistency or settle whether assuming an arbitrary certified method and its domain exhausts the source's capability claim. The additional consistency restriction is concrete, and the capability/domain implication remains unresolved. Accordingly, acceptance is withheld and adjudication is requested rather than labeling a restricted interface theorem faithful-stronger. All judgments use the attached source renderings and inline proof-free evidence only; no tools, proofs, prior judgments or independently recomputed hashes were used.
